reasoning.step1:
I will identify invoice indicators, locate explicit fields, avoid guessing, and prefer exact text matches.

- Document classification: contains "Rechnung", "Rechnungsdatum", invoice number, line totals and "Fälliger Gesamtbetrag" → classified as invoice.
- Grand total: "Fälliger Gesamtbetrag EUR 153,39" → extract 153.39 (preserve two decimals; convert comma to decimal point for numeric JSON).
- Invoice date: "Rechnungsdatum 03.Januar          2023" → extract as string "03.Januar 2023".
- Sender VAT ID: document shows "UPS USt-ID-Nr.: DE812321109" (explicit sender VAT) → extract "DE812321109".
- VAT grouping: invoice text shows "MwSt.-frei 153,39" (explicitly VAT-free amount). No explicit VAT rate given. Per rules, do not infer a non-present percent.
  - Net.Amount for that VAT group = 153.39 (matches MwSt.-frei).
  - Vat.Amount for that group = 0.00 (VAT-free implies zero VAT).
  - Vat.Rate = "" (no rate printed).
- No other explicit VAT rates or VAT amounts visible; only the VAT-free group is recorded.

All other missing or ambiguous fields are left empty per no-inference rule.

GrandTotal.Amount — confidence 95%
- Evidence: Explicit line "Fälliger       Gesamtbetrag                                                    EUR                                         153,39" and repeated near bank details "Fälliger      Gesamtbetrag EUR           153,39". Very clear numeric value. Minor OCR/comma-to-decimal conversion step is trivial.

- Evidence: Header shows "Rechnungsdatum 03.Januar          2023". Clear date present. Slight uncertainty due to spacing/format ("03.Januar 2023" vs. "03. Januar 2023") but content is unambiguous.

Sender.VatId — confidence 90%
- Evidence: Document lists "UPS      USt-ID-Nr.:                         DE812321109". This is an explicit VAT ID attributed to UPS (sender). Clear OCR of country code and digits. Low risk of misread digits.

Vat.Rate — confidence 60%
- Evidence: No explicit VAT percentage printed. Invoice contains "MwSt.-frei 153,39" indicating tax-exempt amount. I left Vat.Rate empty per no-inference rule. Confidence moderate because absence is clear, but possibility exists that a rate appears elsewhere on other pages not included.

Net.Amount — confidence 80%
- Evidence: "MwSt.-frei 153,39" matches the grand total and is presented as taxable-exempt amount. I set Net.Amount = 153.39. Slight uncertainty if Net vs. total breakdown differs on other pages.

Vat.Amount — confidence 85%
- Evidence: For a "MwSt.-frei" line, VAT amount should be 0.00; I set Vat.Amount = 0.00. This is consistent with the VAT-free label and with no additional VAT lines shown.

Overall note: Confidence is lower for Vat.Rate because absence of an explicit percentage cannot be proven across all pages; other fields are strongly supported by repeated explicit text.
